questions.question_fa: خانم 35 سالهای بدون بیماری زمینهای با درد شدید در ناحیه ی RUQ به اورژانس مراجعه میکند. درد وی از دو ساعت قبل شروع شده و با تزریق مخدر وریدی کاهش یافت. در سونوگرافی سنگهای متعدد 5 میلی متری در کیسه صفرا دیده شد و مجاری صفراوی داخل و خارج کبدی نرمال است. چه اقدام درمانی را توصیه میکنید؟
questions.question_en: A 35-year-old woman with no underlying disease comes to the emergency room with severe pain in the RUQ region. His pain started two hours ago and was reduced by intravenous narcotic injection. In the ultrasound, multiple 5 mm stones were seen in the gallbladder, and intrahepatic and extrahepatic bile ducts are normal. What treatment do you recommend?
options_why_fa: نادرست است؛ دلیل رد: «Open Cholecystectomy» در مقایسه با پاسخ صحیح و شرایط بالینی بیمار در هاریسون، اقدام اولویت‌دار یا انتخاب اول بالینی محسوب نمی‌شود.
صحیح است؛ «Laparascopic Cholecystectomy» منطبق بر رفرنس رسمی (اصول طب داخلی هاریسون (ویرایش ۲۲)، بخش اختلالات دستگاه گوارش و کبد و پانکراس)، پاسخ صحیح و مسیر بالینی استاندارد است.

questions.explanation_fa:
تحلیل بالینی و صورت مسئله: در این سناریو، بیمار با تظاهرات «خانم 35 سالهای بدون بیماری زمینهای با درد شدید در ناحیه ی RUQ به اورژانس مراجعه میکند. درد وی از دو ساعت قبل شروع شده و با تزریق مخدر وریدی کاهش یافت. در سونوگرافی سنگهای متعدد 5 میلی متری در کیسه صفرا دیده شد و مجاری صفراوی داخل و خارج کبدی نرمال است. چه اقدام درمانی را توصیه میکنید؟» در حیطه تخصصی گوارش تحت ارزیابی قرار گرفته است. با استناد به مبانی تشخیصی و تصمیم‌گیری بالینی مرجع کانونی اصول طب داخلی هاریسون (ویرایش ۲۲)، بخش اختلالات دستگاه گوارش و کبد و پانکراس، اقدام انتخابی و پاسخ صحیح بالینی «Laparascopic Cholecystectomy» می‌باشد.

پاتوفیزیولوژی و استدلال گایدلاین هاریسون: انتخاب «Laparascopic Cholecystectomy» بر اساس رویکرد گام‌به‌گام طب مبتنی بر شواهد استوار است. این استراتژی درمانی/تشخیصی با هدف تثبیت وضعیت همودینامیک، مهار فرآیندهای پاتولوژیک زمینه‌ای و کاهش مورتالیتی و موربیدیتی ناشی از بیماری اتخاذ می‌گردد. در مدیریت بالینی این بیماری، توازن دقیق میان منافع مداخله و خطرات عوارض جانبی مطابق سرفصل‌های به‌روزشده هاریسون برقرار شده است.

ارزیابی تحلیلی گزینه‌های دیگر: سایر گزینه‌ها به دلیل اثربخشی کمتر، تطابق ناکافی با معیارهای قطعی راهنماهای بالینی، یا داشتن عوارض جانبی و تأخیر در روند بهبودی در مقایسه با «Laparascopic Cholecystectomy» در اولویت بعدی قرار گرفته و رد می‌شوند.
questions.explanation_en: Asymptomatic gallstones usually require observation, and prophylactic cholecystectomy is considered only in selected conditions such as porcelain gallbladder, large polyp, hemolytic anemia, or specific transplant/high-risk. Obesity, rapid weight loss, female sex and cirrhosis increase the risk of stones. Acute cholecystitis with RUQ pain, fever, Murphy and wall thickening/stones requires early laparoscopic cholecystectomy treatment. Renal failure is not the only indication for prophylactic surgery. UDCA is selected for small cholesterol stones in non-surgical patients with high recurrence.

questions.explanation_en: SAAG = serum albumin − ascitic albumin; A value of ≥1.1 indicates portal hypertension. High protein ascites with high SAAG leads to cardiac ascites, Budd-Chiari or early sinusoidal disease, and low protein leads to cirrhosis. SBP is diagnosed with PMN≥250/mm³ and treated immediately with cefotaxime/ceftriaxone; Bedside culture is taken before antibiotic. IV albumin in SBP with renal dysfunction/high bilirubin reduces the risk of HRS, but criteria are needed. Routine endoscopy is not an immediate action for an SBP episode unless there is a separate bleeding/screening indication.

questions.explanation_en: H. pylori is detected by urea breath test or active stool antigen and its eradication is confirmed by non-serological test at least four weeks after antibiotic and two weeks after stopping PPI. IgG remains positive for months/years after treatment and is not a test-of-cure. The choice of regimen depends on clarithromycin resistance and previous exposure; bismuth quadruple therapy is the preferred empirical choice in many areas. gastric ulcer should have endoscopy and biopsy from the edge to rule out malignancy and follow-up healing; Simple duodenal ulcer is more benign. Visible vessel bleeding ulcer requires endoscopic treatment and high-dose IV PPI.

تحلیل بالینی و صورت مسئله: در این سناریو، بیمار با تظاهرات «خانم 47 سالهای با هماتوشزی شدید به اورژانس بیمارستان مراجعه کرده است. در بدو ورود فشار خون خوابیده ی بیمار 130/85mmHg و فشار خون نشسته ی وی 100/70mmHg است. در این مرحله اقدام مناسب جهت بیمار کدام است؟» در حیطه تخصصی گوارش تحت ارزیابی قرار گرفته است. با استناد به مبانی تشخیصی و تصمیم‌گیری بالینی مرجع کانونی اصول طب داخلی هاریسون (ویرایش ۲۲)، بخش اختلالات دستگاه گوارش و کبد و پانکراس، اقدام انتخابی و پاسخ صحیح بالینی «آندوسکوپی فوقانی» می‌باشد.

پاتوفیزیولوژی و استدلال گایدلاین هاریسون: انتخاب «آندوسکوپی فوقانی» بر اساس رویکرد گام‌به‌گام طب مبتنی بر شواهد استوار است. این استراتژی درمانی/تشخیصی با هدف تثبیت وضعیت همودینامیک، مهار فرآیندهای پاتولوژیک زمینه‌ای و کاهش مورتالیتی و موربیدیتی ناشی از بیماری اتخاذ می‌گردد. در مدیریت بالینی این بیماری، توازن دقیق میان منافع مداخله و خطرات عوارض جانبی مطابق سرفصل‌های به‌روزشده هاریسون برقرار شده است.

ارزیابی تحلیلی گزینه‌های دیگر: سایر گزینه‌ها به دلیل اثربخشی کمتر، تطابق ناکافی با معیارهای قطعی راهنماهای بالینی، یا داشتن عوارض جانبی و تأخیر در روند بهبودی در مقایسه با «آندوسکوپی فوقانی» در اولویت بعدی قرار گرفته و رد می‌شوند.
questions.explanation_en: In GI bleeding, first ABC, two IV, type/cross, CBC/coag and resuscitation are performed; Endoscopy is not performed before hemodynamic stabilization. Hematochezia with shock and very high BUN/Cr can be upper GI brisk bleeding, and upper endoscopy is the priority after stabilization. In persistent lower bleeding, colonoscopy after bowel prep; In ongoing brisk bleed, CT angiography and then embolization is useful. A visible hemorrhoid in a person over 45 or with anemia/change bowel habit does not rule out cancer and colonoscopy is necessary. NSAID raises bleeding risk and melena upper source.

UC flare must be differentiated from CMV, C. difficile, amoebiasis, and medication.

Fecal elastase is a non-invasive test and secretin stimulation is more sensitive but invasive/hardly available. Acute pancreatitis with early enteral feeding, analgesia and fluid goal-directed management and antibiotic prophylaxis is not routine.

IgG remains positive for months/years after treatment and is not a test-of-cure. The choice of regimen depends on clarithromycin resistance and previous exposure; bismuth quadruple therapy is the preferred empirical choice in many areas. gastric ulcer should have endoscopy and biopsy from the edge to rule out malignancy and follow-up healing; Simple duodenal ulcer is more benign. Visible vessel bleeding ulcer requires endoscopic treatment and high-dose IV PPI.

In mild biliary pancreatitis, cholecystectomy reduces same admission recurrence and ERCP requires only cholangitis/ongoing obstruction.

questions.explanation_en: In acute diarrhea, dehydration, sepsis, blood, high fever, age and immune status are evaluated first. Most short-term watery cases are treated with ORS and continued feeding, and antibiotics or routine stool testing are not required. questions.explanation_en: Chronic pancreatitis, especially with alcohol, causes pancreatic exocrine insufficiency, smelly/bulky steatorrhea, weight loss, and fat-soluble vitamin deficiency. Fecal elastase is a non-invasive test and secretin stimulation is more sensitive but invasive/hardly available. Treatment is alcohol/smoking cessation, pancreatic enzymes along with food and nutrition. High pleural fluid amylase is seen in pancreatitis/pseudocyst, esophageal rupture and some malignancies, and TB is less important. Acute pancreatitis with early enteral feeding, analgesia and fluid goal-directed management and antibiotic prophylaxis is not routine.

questions.explanation_en: H. pylori is detected by urea breath test or active stool antigen and its eradication is confirmed by non-serological test at least four weeks after antibiotic and two weeks after stopping PPI. IgG remains positive for months/years after treatment and is not a test-of-cure. The choice of regimen depends on clarithromycin resistance and previous exposure; bismuth quadruple therapy is the preferred empirical choice in many areas. gastric ulcer should have endoscopy and biopsy from the edge to rule out malignancy and follow-up healing; Simple duodenal ulcer is more benign. Visible vessel bleeding ulcer requires endoscopic treatment and high-dose IV PPI.

questions.explanation_en: SAAG = serum albumin − ascitic albumin; A value of ≥1.1 indicates portal hypertension. High protein ascites with high SAAG leads to cardiac ascites, Budd-Chiari or early sinusoidal disease, and low protein leads to cirrhosis. SBP is diagnosed with PMN≥250/mm³ and treated immediately with cefotaxime/ceftriaxone; Bedside culture is taken before antibiotic. IV albumin in SBP with renal dysfunction/high bilirubin reduces the risk of HRS, but criteria are needed. Routine endoscopy is not an immediate action for an SBP episode unless there is a separate bleeding/screening indication.

Hematochezia with shock and very high BUN/Cr can be upper GI brisk bleeding, and upper endoscopy is the priority after stabilization. questions.explanation_en: H. pylori is detected by urea breath test or active stool antigen and its eradication is confirmed by non-serological test at least four weeks after antibiotic and two weeks after stopping PPI. IgG remains positive for months/years after treatment and is not a test-of-cure. The choice of regimen depends on clarithromycin resistance and previous exposure; bismuth quadruple therapy is the preferred empirical choice in many areas. gastric ulcer should have endoscopy and biopsy from the edge to rule out malignancy and follow-up healing; Simple duodenal ulcer is more benign. Visible vessel bleeding ulcer requires endoscopic treatment and high-dose IV PPI.

questions.explanation_en: In acute HBV, HBsAg and anti-HBc IgM are positive and anti-HBs is negative; HBeAg shows proliferation but may be negative in precore mutant. The window period is known only with anti-HBc IgM and isolated anti-HBs after vaccination. Acute hepatitis B is often treated in supportive adults; Antiviral is selected for acute liver failure or severe/protracted disease. PT/INR, mental status, glucose and bilirubin determine the severity. HBV DNA is important for baseline/chronic disease management, not a requirement for acute serological diagnosis in all patients.

questions.explanation_en: SAAG = serum albumin − ascitic albumin; A value of ≥1.1 indicates portal hypertension. High protein ascites with high SAAG leads to cardiac ascites, Budd-Chiari or early sinusoidal disease, and low protein leads to cirrhosis. SBP is diagnosed with PMN≥250/mm³ and treated immediately with cefotaxime/ceftriaxone; Bedside culture is taken before antibiotic. IV albumin in SBP with renal dysfunction/high bilirubin reduces the risk of HRS, but criteria are needed. Routine endoscopy is not an immediate action for an SBP episode unless there is a separate bleeding/screening indication.

IgG remains positive for months/years after treatment and is not a test-of-cure. The choice of regimen depends on clarithromycin resistance and previous exposure; bismuth quadruple therapy is the preferred empirical choice in many areas. gastric ulcer should have endoscopy and biopsy from the edge to rule out malignancy and follow-up healing; Simple duodenal ulcer is more benign. Visible vessel bleeding ulcer requires endoscopic treatment and high-dose IV PPI.

تحلیل بالینی و صورت مسئله: در این سناریو، بیمار با تظاهرات «کدام آنتی بادی زیر نقش محافظت کننده در برابر عفونت مجدد هپاتیت ویروسی را دارد؟» در حیطه تخصصی گوارش تحت ارزیابی قرار گرفته است. با استناد به مبانی تشخیصی و تصمیم‌گیری بالینی مرجع کانونی اصول طب داخلی هاریسون (ویرایش ۲۲)، بخش اختلالات دستگاه گوارش و کبد و پانکراس، اقدام انتخابی و پاسخ صحیح بالینی «HAV- Ab- IgG» می‌باشد.

پاتوفیزیولوژی و استدلال گایدلاین هاریسون: انتخاب «HAV- Ab- IgG» بر اساس رویکرد گام‌به‌گام طب مبتنی بر شواهد استوار است. این استراتژی درمانی/تشخیصی با هدف تثبیت وضعیت همودینامیک، مهار فرآیندهای پاتولوژیک زمینه‌ای و کاهش مورتالیتی و موربیدیتی ناشی از بیماری اتخاذ می‌گردد. در مدیریت بالینی این بیماری، توازن دقیق میان منافع مداخله و خطرات عوارض جانبی مطابق سرفصل‌های به‌روزشده هاریسون برقرار شده است.

ارزیابی تحلیلی گزینه‌های دیگر: سایر گزینه‌ها به دلیل اثربخشی کمتر، تطابق ناکافی با معیارهای قطعی راهنماهای بالینی، یا داشتن عوارض جانبی و تأخیر در روند بهبودی در مقایسه با «HAV- Ab- IgG» در اولویت بعدی قرار گرفته و رد می‌شوند.
questions.explanation_en: HAV and HEV are fecal-oral and usually acute self-limited; anti-HAV IgM indicates acute infection and total/IgG remote immunity. HAV does not become chronic and the treatment is supportive. HCV is mainly blood-borne; It shows anti-HCV exposure and HCV RNA active infection. New guidelines recommend DAA treatment after acute HCV diagnosis and do not wait long for spontaneous clearance. HBV markers should be interpreted separately; "Total HAV antibody" does not prove acute disease.

questions.question_en: A 45-year-old man was referred because of jaundice that started a week ago. The patient had a history of stomach cancer and subsequent surgery. He is currently undergoing the sixth round of chemotherapy. He has a history of transient jaundice as a child, but he has no history of liver disease in his first-degree relatives. The result of the initial test is as follows: AST = 980 (NL: up to 40) ALT = 1150 (NL: up to 40) Alkp = 380 (NL: up to 306) Bili (T) = 18, Bili (D) = 11 HBS Ab+, HBC Ab IgG+, Ceruloplasmin = 25 (15-40) Which diagnosis is more likely?

High protein ascites with high SAAG leads to cardiac ascites, Budd-Chiari or early sinusoidal disease, and low protein leads to cirrhosis. SBP is diagnosed with PMN≥250/mm³ and treated immediately with cefotaxime/ceftriaxone; Bedside culture is taken before antibiotic. IV albumin in SBP with renal dysfunction/high bilirubin reduces the risk of HRS, but criteria are needed. Routine endoscopy is not an immediate action for an SBP episode unless there is a separate bleeding/screening indication.

questions.explanation_en: In GI bleeding, first ABC, two IV, type/cross, CBC/coag and resuscitation are performed; Endoscopy is not performed before hemodynamic stabilization. In persistent lower bleeding, colonoscopy after bowel prep; In ongoing brisk bleed, CT angiography and then embolization is useful. A visible hemorrhoid in a person over 45 or with anemia/change bowel habit does not rule out cancer and colonoscopy is necessary. NSAID raises bleeding risk and melena upper source.

questions.explanation_en: Average-risk CRC screening starts at the age of 45. In first-degree relative with CRC or advanced adenoma before age 60, colonoscopy is recommended starting at age 40 or 10 years earlier than family diagnosis—whichever is earlier—and every 5 years. If the mother is infected at the age of 26, hereditary syndrome such as Lynch/FAP should be investigated with genetic counseling and the usual options may not be correct. CEA is not enough for initial screening/diagnosis, but it is useful for baseline prognostic and surveillance after treatment. Rectal bleeding in old age with hemorrhoids also requires colon evaluation.

questions.explanation_en: Portal hypertension is clinically significant with HVPG≥10 mmHg and cirrhosis is associated with high intrahepatic resistance and splanchnic vasodilation, hyperdynamic circulation and high cardiac output. Varices, ascites, splenomegaly/hypersplenism and encephalopathy are complications. Variceal bleeding is treated with vasoactive drugs, antibiotics, endoscopic banding and careful resuscitation. If there are varices with normal liver and synthetic function and splenomegaly, portal/splenic vein thrombosis or noncirrhotic portal hypertension is checked with Doppler. Child-Pugh requires bilirubin, albumin, INR, ascites and encephalopathy and cannot be calculated without all data.

questions.explanation_en: In acute HBV, HBsAg and anti-HBc IgM are positive and anti-HBs is negative; HBeAg shows proliferation but may be negative in precore mutant. The window period is known only with anti-HBc IgM and isolated anti-HBs after vaccination. Acute hepatitis B is often treated in supportive adults; Antiviral is selected for acute liver failure or severe/protracted disease. PT/INR, mental status, glucose and bilirubin determine the severity. HBV DNA is important for baseline/chronic disease management, not a requirement for acute serological diagnosis in all patients.

questions.explanation_en: Asymptomatic gallstones usually require observation, and prophylactic cholecystectomy is considered only in selected conditions such as porcelain gallbladder, large polyp, hemolytic anemia, or specific transplant/high-risk. Obesity, rapid weight loss, female sex and cirrhosis increase the risk of stones. Acute cholecystitis with RUQ pain, fever, Murphy and wall thickening/stones requires early laparoscopic cholecystectomy treatment. Renal failure is not the only indication for prophylactic surgery. UDCA is selected for small cholesterol stones in non-surgical patients with high recurrence.

questions.explanation_en: In acute diarrhea, dehydration, sepsis, blood, high fever, age and immune status are evaluated first. Most short-term watery cases are treated with ORS and continued feeding, and antibiotics or routine stool testing are not required. Stool culture/PCR is relevant in dysentery, severe fever, severe dehydration, outbreak, immunocompromise, old age or persistence, and C. difficile testing after antibiotic/hospitalization. Loperamide is avoided in bloody diarrhea, high fever or suspected invasive infection. Diagnostic workup should not delay rehydration.

questions.explanation_en: In GI bleeding, first ABC, two IV, type/cross, CBC/coag and resuscitation are performed; Endoscopy is not performed before hemodynamic stabilization. Hematochezia with shock and very high BUN/Cr can be upper GI brisk bleeding, and upper endoscopy is the priority after stabilization. In persistent lower bleeding, colonoscopy after bowel prep; In ongoing brisk bleed, CT angiography and then embolization is useful. A visible hemorrhoid in a person over 45 or with anemia/change bowel habit does not rule out cancer and colonoscopy is necessary. NSAID raises bleeding risk and melena upper source.

questions.explanation_en: In acute HBV, HBsAg and anti-HBc IgM are positive and anti-HBs is negative; HBeAg shows proliferation but may be negative in precore mutant. The window period is known only with anti-HBc IgM and isolated anti-HBs after vaccination. Acute hepatitis B is often treated in supportive adults; Antiviral is selected for acute liver failure or severe/protracted disease. PT/INR, mental status, glucose and bilirubin determine the severity. HBV DNA is important for baseline/chronic disease management, not a requirement for acute serological diagnosis in all patients.

questions.explanation_en: Pruritus, direct hyperbilirubinemia and high ALP/GGT with ultrasound ducts suggest normal intrahepatic cholestasis. Most middle-aged women have PBC, AMA positive and small intrahepatic duct destruction; With cholestatic enzymes and AMA, biopsy is usually not required for diagnosis unless there is overlap/uncertainty. questions.explanation_en: SAAG = serum albumin − ascitic albumin; A value of ≥1.1 indicates portal hypertension. High protein ascites with high SAAG leads to cardiac ascites, Budd-Chiari or early sinusoidal disease, and low protein leads to cirrhosis. SBP is diagnosed with PMN≥250/mm³ and treated immediately with cefotaxime/ceftriaxone; Bedside culture is taken before antibiotic. IV albumin in SBP with renal dysfunction/high bilirubin reduces the risk of HRS, but criteria are needed. Routine endoscopy is not an immediate action for an SBP episode unless there is a separate bleeding/screening indication.

questions.explanation_en: In GI bleeding, first ABC, two IV, type/cross, CBC/coag and resuscitation are performed; Endoscopy is not performed before hemodynamic stabilization. Hematochezia with shock and very high BUN/Cr can be upper GI brisk bleeding, and upper endoscopy is the priority after stabilization. In persistent lower bleeding, colonoscopy after bowel prep; In ongoing brisk bleed, CT angiography and then embolization is useful. A visible hemorrhoid in a person over 45 or with anemia/change bowel habit does not rule out cancer and colonoscopy is necessary. NSAID raises bleeding risk and melena upper source.

questions.explanation_en: Asymptomatic gallstones usually require observation, and prophylactic cholecystectomy is considered only in selected conditions such as porcelain gallbladder, large polyp, hemolytic anemia, or specific transplant/high-risk. Obesity, rapid weight loss, female sex and cirrhosis increase the risk of stones. Acute cholecystitis with RUQ pain, fever, Murphy and wall thickening/stones requires early laparoscopic cholecystectomy treatment. Renal failure is not the only indication for prophylactic surgery. UDCA is selected for small cholesterol stones in non-surgical patients with high recurrence.

Acute cholecystitis with RUQ pain, fever, Murphy and wall thickening/stones requires early laparoscopic cholecystectomy treatment. Renal failure is not the only indication for prophylactic surgery. UDCA is selected for small cholesterol stones in non-surgical patients with high recurrence.

چرا «اریتم ندوزوم» صحیح است: اریتم ندوزوم (Erythema Nodosum) از تظاهرات خارج روده‌ای شاخص در بیماری التهابی روده است که به طور موازی و مستقیم با شدت فعالیت بیماری روده تغییر می‌کند. این انتخاب دقیقاً با معیارهای تشخیصی منبع: هاریسون ۲۲، فصل مربوطه هم‌سو است و بیشترین سود با کمترین خطر را دارد.

رد سایر گزینه‌ها: گزینه 1 (آرتریت مفاصل محیطی): آرتریت محیطی نوع ۱ با فعالیت مرتبط است ولی اریتم ندوزوم به صورت کامل و تیپیک با شعله‌وری فعالیت الته؛ گزینه 2 (کالنژیت اسکلروزان اولیه): کلانژیت اسکلروزان اولیه (PSC) سیری مستقل از فعالیت التهابی کولیت دارد.؛ گزینه 3 (ساکروایلئیت): ساکروایلئیت سیر با…. هر یک یا با یافته‌های اصلی ناسازگار است یا در الگوریتم جایگاه بعدی دارد یا بدون مزیت اضافی خطر/هزینه می‌افزاید.

questions.explanation_en: Crohn's transmural and skip lesions from mouth to anus, terminal ileum is a common involvement and noncaseating granuloma is possible; Fistula, stricture, perianal disease and malabsorption are common. Stool shows RBC/WBC or calprotectin/lactoferrin inflammation, and IBS does not have such inflammatory evidence. Yersinia causes terminal ileitis and clinical Crohn's mimic.

questions.explanation_en: H. pylori is detected by urea breath test or active stool antigen and its eradication is confirmed by non-serological test at least four weeks after antibiotic and two weeks after stopping PPI. IgG remains positive for months/years after treatment and is not a test-of-cure. The choice of regimen depends on clarithromycin resistance and previous exposure; bismuth quadruple therapy is the preferred empirical choice in many areas. gastric ulcer should have endoscopy and biopsy from the edge to rule out malignancy and follow-up healing; Simple duodenal ulcer is more benign. Visible vessel bleeding ulcer requires endoscopic treatment and high-dose IV PPI.

questions.explanation_en: Portal hypertension is clinically significant with HVPG≥10 mmHg and cirrhosis is associated with high intrahepatic resistance and splanchnic vasodilation, hyperdynamic circulation and high cardiac output. Varices, ascites, splenomegaly/hypersplenism and encephalopathy are complications. Variceal bleeding is treated with vasoactive drugs, antibiotics, endoscopic banding and careful resuscitation. If there are varices with normal liver and synthetic function and splenomegaly, portal/splenic vein thrombosis or noncirrhotic portal hypertension is checked with Doppler. Child-Pugh requires bilirubin, albumin, INR, ascites and encephalopathy and cannot be calculated without all data.

options_why_fa: صحیح است؛ دیابت شیرین به تنهایی در یک بیمار بدون علامت با سنگ ۲ سانتی‌متری، دیگر طبق راهنماهای مدرن اندیکاسیون کوله‌سیستکتومی پیشگیرانه محسوب نمی‌شود.

questions.explanation_fa:
تحلیل صورت سؤال: محور اصلی در حوزه «داخلی» و مبحث «گوارش» است. صورت سؤال «کدامیک از بیماران زیر نیاز به prophylactic cholecystectomy ندارد؟…» نکته کلیدی را در مرکز قرار می‌دهد. برای پاسخ باید یافته‌ها را با الگوریتم منبع: هاریسون ۲۲، فصل مربوطه تطبیق داد.

چرا «آقای 45 ساله ی دیابتی با سنگ 2 سانتی متری در کیسه صفرا» صحیح است: دیابت شیرین به تنهایی در یک بیمار بدون علامت با سنگ ۲ سانتی‌متری، دیگر طبق راهنماهای مدرن اندیکاسیون کوله‌سیستکتومی پیشگیرانه محسوب نمی‌شود. این انتخاب دقیقاً با معیارهای تشخیصی منبع: هاریسون ۲۲، فصل مربوطه هم‌سو است و بیشترین سود با کمترین خطر را دارد.

رد سایر گزینه‌ها: گزینه 2 (خانم 50 سالهای با سنگ 4 سانتی متری در کیسه صفرا): سنگ‌های صفراوی بزرگتر از ۳ یا ۴ سانتی‌متر به علت افزایش خطر سرطان کیسه صفرا اندیکاسیون جراحی پیشگیرا؛ گزینه 3 (خانم 30 سالهای با سنگ 1 سانتی متری و پولیپ 2 سانتی متری در کیسه صفرا): پولیپ‌های کیسه صفرا بزرگتر از ۱ سانتی‌م…. هر یک یا با یافته‌های اصلی ناسازگار است یا در الگوریتم جایگاه بعدی دارد یا بدون مزیت اضافی خطر/هزینه می‌افزاید.

درسنامه فشرده (منبع: هاریسون ۲۲، فصل مربوطه): ابتدا پایداری همودینامیک، سپس شرح حال هدفمند و معاینه متمرکز، و تست‌های انتخابی بر اساس پیش‌آزمون. درمان بر پایه شدت، زمینه و ترجیح بیمار؛ پایش پاسخ و عوارض ضروری است.

نکته طلایی و دام: گزینه «درستِ ناقص» شایع‌ترین دام است؛ کامل‌ترین تطابق با رفرنس را انتخاب کنید. مراقب قیدهای «همیشه/هرگز» باشید — در پزشکی مطلق نادر است.
questions.explanation_en: Asymptomatic gallstones usually require observation, and prophylactic cholecystectomy is considered only in selected conditions such as porcelain gallbladder, large polyp, hemolytic anemia, or specific transplant/high-risk. Obesity, rapid weight loss, female sex and cirrhosis increase the risk of stones. Acute cholecystitis with RUQ pain, fever, Murphy and wall thickening/stones requires early laparoscopic cholecystectomy treatment. Renal failure is not the only indication for prophylactic surgery. UDCA is selected for small cholesterol stones in non-surgical patients with high recurrence.

questions.explanation_en: SAAG = serum albumin − ascitic albumin; A value of ≥1.1 indicates portal hypertension. High protein ascites with high SAAG leads to cardiac ascites, Budd-Chiari or early sinusoidal disease, and low protein leads to cirrhosis. SBP is diagnosed with PMN≥250/mm³ and treated immediately with cefotaxime/ceftriaxone; Bedside culture is taken before antibiotic. IV albumin in SBP with renal dysfunction/high bilirubin reduces the risk of HRS, but criteria are needed. Routine endoscopy is not an immediate action for an SBP episode unless there is a separate bleeding/screening indication.

questions.explanation_en: In acute HBV, HBsAg and anti-HBc IgM are positive and anti-HBs is negative; HBeAg shows proliferation but may be negative in precore mutant. The window period is known only with anti-HBc IgM and isolated anti-HBs after vaccination. Acute hepatitis B is often treated in supportive adults; Antiviral is selected for acute liver failure or severe/protracted disease. PT/INR, mental status, glucose and bilirubin determine the severity. HBV DNA is important for baseline/chronic disease management, not a requirement for acute serological diagnosis in all patients.

questions.explanation_en: In GI bleeding, first ABC, two IV, type/cross, CBC/coag and resuscitation are performed; Endoscopy is not performed before hemodynamic stabilization. Hematochezia with shock and very high BUN/Cr can be upper GI brisk bleeding, and upper endoscopy is the priority after stabilization. In persistent lower bleeding, colonoscopy after bowel prep; In ongoing brisk bleed, CT angiography and then embolization is useful. A visible hemorrhoid in a person over 45 or with anemia/change bowel habit does not rule out cancer and colonoscopy is necessary. NSAID raises bleeding risk and melena upper source.

questions.explanation_en: In acute HBV, HBsAg and anti-HBc IgM are positive and anti-HBs is negative; HBeAg shows proliferation but may be negative in precore mutant. The window period is known only with anti-HBc IgM and isolated anti-HBs after vaccination. Acute hepatitis B is often treated in supportive adults; Antiviral is selected for acute liver failure or severe/protracted disease. PT/INR, mental status, glucose and bilirubin determine the severity. HBV DNA is important for baseline/chronic disease management, not a requirement for acute serological diagnosis in all patients.

questions.explanation_en: Portal hypertension is clinically significant with HVPG≥10 mmHg and cirrhosis is associated with high intrahepatic resistance and splanchnic vasodilation, hyperdynamic circulation and high cardiac output. Varices, ascites, splenomegaly/hypersplenism and encephalopathy are complications. Variceal bleeding is treated with vasoactive drugs, antibiotics, endoscopic banding and careful resuscitation. If there are varices with normal liver and synthetic function and splenomegaly, portal/splenic vein thrombosis or noncirrhotic portal hypertension is checked with Doppler. Child-Pugh requires bilirubin, albumin, INR, ascites and encephalopathy and cannot be calculated without all data.

questions.explanation_en: SAAG = serum albumin − ascitic albumin; A value of ≥1.1 indicates portal hypertension. High protein ascites with high SAAG leads to cardiac ascites, Budd-Chiari or early sinusoidal disease, and low protein leads to cirrhosis. SBP is diagnosed with PMN≥250/mm³ and treated immediately with cefotaxime/ceftriaxone; Bedside culture is taken before antibiotic. IV albumin in SBP with renal dysfunction/high bilirubin reduces the risk of HRS, but criteria are needed. Routine endoscopy is not an immediate action for an SBP episode unless there is a separate bleeding/screening indication.

questions.explanation_en: In acute HBV, HBsAg and anti-HBc IgM are positive and anti-HBs is negative; HBeAg shows proliferation but may be negative in precore mutant. The window period is known only with anti-HBc IgM and isolated anti-HBs after vaccination. Acute hepatitis B is often treated in supportive adults; Antiviral is selected for acute liver failure or severe/protracted disease. PT/INR, mental status, glucose and bilirubin determine the severity. HBV DNA is important for baseline/chronic disease management, not a requirement for acute serological diagnosis in all patients.

The primary treatment is goal-directed lactated Ringer, analgesia and early oral/enteral feeding; A fixed volume of 5-6 liters is dangerous for everyone. Antibiotic prophylaxis is prohibited in sterile necrosis. infected necrosis is managed with antibiotic penetrating necrosis and step-up approach including drainage and delayed minimally invasive necrosectomy; Immediate open surgery is usually not preferred. In mild biliary pancreatitis, cholecystectomy reduces same admission recurrence and ERCP requires only cholangitis/ongoing obstruction.

questions.explanation_en: Chronic pancreatitis, especially with alcohol, causes pancreatic exocrine insufficiency, smelly/bulky steatorrhea, weight loss, and fat-soluble vitamin deficiency. Fecal elastase is a non-invasive test and secretin stimulation is more sensitive but invasive/hardly available. Treatment is alcohol/smoking cessation, pancreatic enzymes along with food and nutrition. High pleural fluid amylase is seen in pancreatitis/pseudocyst, esophageal rupture and some malignancies, and TB is less important. Acute pancreatitis with early enteral feeding, analgesia and fluid goal-directed management and antibiotic prophylaxis is not routine.

questions.explanation_en: SAAG = serum albumin − ascitic albumin; A value of ≥1.1 indicates portal hypertension. High protein ascites with high SAAG leads to cardiac ascites, Budd-Chiari or early sinusoidal disease, and low protein leads to cirrhosis. SBP is diagnosed with PMN≥250/mm³ and treated immediately with cefotaxime/ceftriaxone; Bedside culture is taken before antibiotic. IV albumin in SBP with renal dysfunction/high bilirubin reduces the risk of HRS, but criteria are needed. Routine endoscopy is not an immediate action for an SBP episode unless there is a separate bleeding/screening indication.

پاتوفیزیولوژی و استدلال گایدلاین هاریسون: انتخاب «اقدام بیشتری توصیه نمیشود» بر اساس رویکرد گام‌به‌گام طب مبتنی بر شواهد استوار است. این استراتژی درمانی/تشخیصی با هدف تثبیت وضعیت همودینامیک، مهار فرآیندهای پاتولوژیک زمینه‌ای و کاهش مورتالیتی و موربیدیتی ناشی از بیماری اتخاذ می‌گردد. در مدیریت بالینی این بیماری، توازن دقیق میان منافع مداخله و خطرات عوارض جانبی مطابق سرفصل‌های به‌روزشده هاریسون برقرار شده است.

ارزیابی تحلیلی گزینه‌های دیگر: سایر گزینه‌ها به دلیل اثربخشی کمتر، تطابق ناکافی با معیارهای قطعی راهنماهای بالینی، یا داشتن عوارض جانبی و تأخیر در روند بهبودی در مقایسه با «اقدام بیشتری توصیه نمیشود» در اولویت بعدی قرار گرفته و رد می‌شوند.
questions.explanation_en: In GI bleeding, first ABC, two IV, type/cross, CBC/coag and resuscitation are performed; Endoscopy is not performed before hemodynamic stabilization. Hematochezia with shock and very high BUN/Cr can be upper GI brisk bleeding, and upper endoscopy is the priority after stabilization. In persistent lower bleeding, colonoscopy after bowel prep; In ongoing brisk bleed, CT angiography and then embolization is useful. A visible hemorrhoid in a person over 45 or with anemia/change bowel habit does not rule out cancer and colonoscopy is necessary. NSAID raises bleeding risk and melena upper source.

questions.explanation_en: H. pylori is detected by urea breath test or active stool antigen and its eradication is confirmed by non-serological test at least four weeks after antibiotic and two weeks after stopping PPI. IgG remains positive for months/years after treatment and is not a test-of-cure. The choice of regimen depends on clarithromycin resistance and previous exposure; bismuth quadruple therapy is the preferred empirical choice in many areas. gastric ulcer should have endoscopy and biopsy from the edge to rule out malignancy and follow-up healing; Simple duodenal ulcer is more benign. Visible vessel bleeding ulcer requires endoscopic treatment and high-dose IV PPI.

questions.explanation_en: In acute HBV, HBsAg and anti-HBc IgM are positive and anti-HBs is negative; HBeAg shows proliferation but may be negative in precore mutant. The window period is known only with anti-HBc IgM and isolated anti-HBs after vaccination. Acute hepatitis B is often treated in supportive adults; Antiviral is selected for acute liver failure or severe/protracted disease. PT/INR, mental status, glucose and bilirubin determine the severity. HBV DNA is important for baseline/chronic disease management, not a requirement for acute serological diagnosis in all patients.

questions.explanation_en: SAAG = serum albumin − ascitic albumin; A value of ≥1.1 indicates portal hypertension. High protein ascites with high SAAG leads to cardiac ascites, Budd-Chiari or early sinusoidal disease, and low protein leads to cirrhosis. SBP is diagnosed with PMN≥250/mm³ and treated immediately with cefotaxime/ceftriaxone; Bedside culture is taken before antibiotic. IV albumin in SBP with renal dysfunction/high bilirubin reduces the risk of HRS, but criteria are needed. Routine endoscopy is not an immediate action for an SBP episode unless there is a separate bleeding/screening indication.

questions.explanation_fa:
تحلیل صورت سؤال: محور اصلی در حوزه «داخلی» و مبحث «گوارش» است. صورت سؤال «آقایی 45 ساله با نتایج آزمایشات زیر به شما مراجعه میکند. HBsHg: negative, Anti H…» نکته کلیدی را در مرکز قرار می‌دهد. برای پاسخ باید یافته‌ها را با الگوریتم منبع: هاریسون ۲۲، فصل مربوطه تطبیق داد.

چرا «Chronic hepatitis B» صحیح است: هپاتیت B مزمن با منفی بودن HBsAg به طور قطعی رد می‌شود، زیرا برای تشخیص هپاتیت مزمن مثبت بودن HBsAg برای حداقل ۶ ماه الزامی است. این انتخاب دقیقاً با معیارهای تشخیصی منبع: هاریسون ۲۲، فصل مربوطه هم‌سو است و بیشترین سود با کمترین خطر را دارد.

رد سایر گزینه‌ها: گزینه 1 (HBV vaccination): با منفی بودن سایر آنتی‌بادی‌ها و مثبت بودن منفرد Anti-HBs، واکسیناسیون هپاتیت B محتمل‌ترین حالت است.؛ گزینه 2 (Hepatitis B in the remote past): در عفونت گذشته ممکن است تیتر آنتی‌بادی‌های مرکزی به مرور کاهش یافته باشد و مطرح است.؛ گزینه 4 (False positive…. هر یک یا با یافته‌های اصلی ناسازگار است یا در الگوریتم جایگاه بعدی دارد یا بدون مزیت اضافی خطر/هزینه می‌افزاید.

درسنامه فشرده (منبع: هاریسون ۲۲، فصل مربوطه): ابتدا پایداری همودینامیک، سپس شرح حال هدفمند و معاینه متمرکز، و تست‌های انتخابی بر اساس پیش‌آزمون. درمان بر پایه شدت، زمینه و ترجیح بیمار؛ پایش پاسخ و عوارض ضروری است.

نکته طلایی و دام: گزینه «درستِ ناقص» شایع‌ترین دام است؛ کامل‌ترین تطابق با رفرنس را انتخاب کنید. مراقب قیدهای «همیشه/هرگز» باشید — در پزشکی مطلق نادر است.
questions.explanation_en: In acute HBV, HBsAg and anti-HBc IgM are positive and anti-HBs is negative; HBeAg shows proliferation but may be negative in precore mutant. The window period is known only with anti-HBc IgM and isolated anti-HBs after vaccination. Acute hepatitis B is often treated in supportive adults; Antiviral is selected for acute liver failure or severe/protracted disease. PT/INR, mental status, glucose and bilirubin determine the severity. HBV DNA is important for baseline/chronic disease management, not a requirement for acute serological diagnosis in all patients.

questions.explanation_en: Acute pancreatitis is diagnosed with epigastric pain radiating to back and lipase/amylase more than three times or imaging. The primary treatment is goal-directed lactated Ringer, analgesia and early oral/enteral feeding; A fixed volume of 5-6 liters is dangerous for everyone. Antibiotic prophylaxis is prohibited in sterile necrosis. infected necrosis is managed with antibiotic penetrating necrosis and step-up approach including drainage and delayed minimally invasive necrosectomy; Immediate open surgery is usually not preferred. In first-degree relative with CRC or advanced adenoma before age 60, colonoscopy is recommended starting at age 40 or 10 years earlier than family diagnosis—whichever is earlier—and every 5 years. questions.explanation_en: H. pylori is detected by urea breath test or active stool antigen and its eradication is confirmed by non-serological test at least four weeks after antibiotic and two weeks after stopping PPI. IgG remains positive for months/years after treatment and is not a test-of-cure. The choice of regimen depends on clarithromycin resistance and previous exposure; bismuth quadruple therapy is the preferred empirical choice in many areas. gastric ulcer should have endoscopy and biopsy from the edge to rule out malignancy and follow-up healing; Simple duodenal ulcer is more benign. Visible vessel bleeding ulcer requires endoscopic treatment and high-dose IV PPI.

options_fa: آقای 55 سالهای بدون ریسک فاکتور و بدون علائم بالینی
خانم 30 سالهای بدون علائم گوارشی که به دلیل آنمی فقر آهن ارجاع شده است.

خانم 40 سالهای بدون عالمت که سابقه ی کانسر کولون در خاله و دایی اش در سن 65 سالگی را ذکر میکند.

درسنامه فشرده (منبع: هاریسون ۲۲، فصل مربوطه): ابتدا پایداری همودینامیک، سپس شرح حال هدفمند و معاینه متمرکز، و تست‌های انتخابی بر اساس پیش‌آزمون. درمان بر پایه شدت، زمینه و ترجیح بیمار؛ پایش پاسخ و عوارض ضروری است.

questions.explanation_en: Average-risk CRC screening starts at the age of 45. In first-degree relative with CRC or advanced adenoma before age 60, colonoscopy is recommended starting at age 40 or 10 years earlier than family diagnosis—whichever is earlier—and every 5 years. If the mother is infected at the age of 26, hereditary syndrome such as Lynch/FAP should be investigated with genetic counseling and the usual options may not be correct. CEA is not enough for initial screening/diagnosis, but it is useful for baseline prognostic and surveillance after treatment. Rectal bleeding in old age with hemorrhoids also requires colon evaluation.

questions.explanation_en: Portal hypertension is clinically significant with HVPG≥10 mmHg and cirrhosis is associated with high intrahepatic resistance and splanchnic vasodilation, hyperdynamic circulation and high cardiac output. Varices, ascites, splenomegaly/hypersplenism and encephalopathy are complications. Variceal bleeding is treated with vasoactive drugs, antibiotics, endoscopic banding and careful resuscitation. If there are varices with normal liver and synthetic function and splenomegaly, portal/splenic vein thrombosis or noncirrhotic portal hypertension is checked with Doppler. Child-Pugh requires bilirubin, albumin, INR, ascites and encephalopathy and cannot be calculated without all data.

questions.explanation_en: H. pylori is detected by urea breath test or active stool antigen and its eradication is confirmed by non-serological test at least four weeks after antibiotic and two weeks after stopping PPI. IgG remains positive for months/years after treatment and is not a test-of-cure. The choice of regimen depends on clarithromycin resistance and previous exposure; bismuth quadruple therapy is the preferred empirical choice in many areas. gastric ulcer should have endoscopy and biopsy from the edge to rule out malignancy and follow-up healing; Simple duodenal ulcer is more benign. Visible vessel bleeding ulcer requires endoscopic treatment and high-dose IV PPI.

questions.explanation_en: In acute HBV, HBsAg and anti-HBc IgM are positive and anti-HBs is negative; HBeAg shows proliferation but may be negative in precore mutant. questions.explanation_en: Acute pancreatitis is diagnosed with epigastric pain radiating to back and lipase/amylase more than three times or imaging. The primary treatment is goal-directed lactated Ringer, analgesia and early oral/enteral feeding; A fixed volume of 5-6 liters is dangerous for everyone. Antibiotic prophylaxis is prohibited in sterile necrosis. infected necrosis is managed with antibiotic penetrating necrosis and step-up approach including drainage and delayed minimally invasive necrosectomy; Immediate open surgery is usually not preferred. In mild biliary pancreatitis, cholecystectomy reduces same admission recurrence and ERCP requires only cholangitis/ongoing obstruction.

questions.explanation_en: Ulcerative colitis is a continuous inflammation of the mucosa from the rectum to the proximal and is associated with bloody diarrhea, urgency and complications such as toxic megacolon, PSC and colorectal cancer. acute severe UC with stool infection/C. difficile/CMV assessment, IV steroid, VTE prophylaxis, plain abdominal radiograph and surgical consultation are managed; Complete colonoscopy and barium enema in toxic megacolon have the risk of perforation. PSC is diagnosed with cholestatic enzymes and MRCP multifocal stricturing; p-ANCA/ANA are not specific and biopsy is selected for small-duct/overlap. UC flare must be differentiated from CMV, C. difficile, amoebiasis, and medication.

questions.explanation_en: Typical GERD is treated without alarm with PPI trial; Endoscopy is necessary in dysphagia, bleeding, anemia, weight loss or refractory symptoms. Ambulatory pH monitoring is used in unclear diagnosis, refractory symptoms with normal endoscopy or before antireflux surgery, but it proves severe erosive esophagitis diagnosis and pH is not necessary for proof. Eosinophilic esophagitis is defined by dysphagia/food impaction and ≥15 eos/hpf; First-line shared decision treatment includes PPI, swallowed topical steroid or elimination diet. Systemic steroid is only selected severe and H2 blocker is not sufficient treatment of EoE.

questions.explanation_en: In acute HBV, HBsAg and anti-HBc IgM are positive and anti-HBs is negative; HBeAg shows proliferation but may be negative in precore mutant. The window period is known only with anti-HBc IgM and isolated anti-HBs after vaccination. Acute hepatitis B is often treated in supportive adults; Antiviral is selected for acute liver failure or severe/protracted disease. questions.explanation_en: In GI bleeding, first ABC, two IV, type/cross, CBC/coag and resuscitation are performed; Endoscopy is not performed before hemodynamic stabilization. Hematochezia with shock and very high BUN/Cr can be upper GI brisk bleeding, and upper endoscopy is the priority after stabilization. In persistent lower bleeding, colonoscopy after bowel prep; In ongoing brisk bleed, CT angiography and then embolization is useful. A visible hemorrhoid in a person over 45 or with anemia/change bowel habit does not rule out cancer and colonoscopy is necessary. NSAID raises bleeding risk and melena upper source.

questions.explanation_en: SAAG = serum albumin − ascitic albumin; A value of ≥1.1 indicates portal hypertension. High protein ascites with high SAAG leads to cardiac ascites, Budd-Chiari or early sinusoidal disease, and low protein leads to cirrhosis. questions.explanation_en: In acute HBV, HBsAg and anti-HBc IgM are positive and anti-HBs is negative; HBeAg shows proliferation but may be negative in precore mutant. The window period is known only with anti-HBc IgM and isolated anti-HBs after vaccination. questions.explanation_en: Average-risk CRC screening starts at the age of 45. In first-degree relative with CRC or advanced adenoma before age 60, colonoscopy is recommended starting at age 40 or 10 years earlier than family diagnosis—whichever is earlier—and every 5 years. If the mother is infected at the age of 26, hereditary syndrome such as Lynch/FAP should be investigated with genetic counseling and the usual options may not be correct. CEA is not enough for initial screening/diagnosis, but it is useful for baseline prognostic and surveillance after treatment. Rectal bleeding in old age with hemorrhoids also requires colon evaluation.

questions.explanation_en: HAV and HEV are fecal-oral and usually acute self-limited; anti-HAV IgM indicates acute infection and total/IgG remote immunity. HAV does not become chronic and the treatment is supportive. HCV is mainly blood-borne; It shows anti-HCV exposure and HCV RNA active infection. New guidelines recommend DAA treatment after acute HCV diagnosis and do not wait long for spontaneous clearance. HBV markers should be interpreted separately; "Total HAV antibody" does not prove acute disease.

questions.explanation_en: In GI bleeding, first ABC, two IV, type/cross, CBC/coag and resuscitation are performed; Endoscopy is not performed before hemodynamic stabilization. Hematochezia with shock and very high BUN/Cr can be upper GI brisk bleeding, and upper endoscopy is the priority after stabilization. In persistent lower bleeding, colonoscopy after bowel prep; In ongoing brisk bleed, CT angiography and then embolization is useful. A visible hemorrhoid in a person over 45 or with anemia/change bowel habit does not rule out cancer and colonoscopy is necessary. NSAID raises bleeding risk and melena upper source.

questions.explanation_en: In acute diarrhea, dehydration, sepsis, blood, high fever, age and immune status are evaluated first. Most short-term watery cases are treated with ORS and continued feeding, and antibiotics or routine stool testing are not required. Stool culture/PCR is relevant in dysentery, severe fever, severe dehydration, outbreak, immunocompromise, old age or persistence, and C. difficile testing after antibiotic/hospitalization. Loperamide is avoided in bloody diarrhea, high fever or suspected invasive infection. Diagnostic workup should not delay rehydration.

پاتوفیزیولوژی و استدلال گایدلاین هاریسون: انتخاب «لیپوم معده» بر اساس رویکرد گام‌به‌گام طب مبتنی بر شواهد استوار است. این استراتژی درمانی/تشخیصی با هدف تثبیت وضعیت همودینامیک، مهار فرآیندهای پاتولوژیک زمینه‌ای و کاهش مورتالیتی و موربیدیتی ناشی از بیماری اتخاذ می‌گردد. در مدیریت بالینی این بیماری، توازن دقیق میان منافع مداخله و خطرات عوارض جانبی مطابق سرفصل‌های به‌روزشده هاریسون برقرار شده است.

ارزیابی تحلیلی گزینه‌های دیگر: سایر گزینه‌ها به دلیل اثربخشی کمتر، تطابق ناکافی با معیارهای قطعی راهنماهای بالینی، یا داشتن عوارض جانبی و تأخیر در روند بهبودی در مقایسه با «لیپوم معده» در اولویت بعدی قرار گرفته و رد می‌شوند.
questions.explanation_en: H. pylori is detected by urea breath test or active stool antigen and its eradication is confirmed by non-serological test at least four weeks after antibiotic and two weeks after stopping PPI. IgG remains positive for months/years after treatment and is not a test-of-cure. The choice of regimen depends on clarithromycin resistance and previous exposure; bismuth quadruple therapy is the preferred empirical choice in many areas. gastric ulcer should have endoscopy and biopsy from the edge to rule out malignancy and follow-up healing; Simple duodenal ulcer is more benign. Visible vessel bleeding ulcer requires endoscopic treatment and high-dose IV PPI.

questions.explanation_en: Portal hypertension is clinically significant with HVPG≥10 mmHg and cirrhosis is associated with high intrahepatic resistance and splanchnic vasodilation, hyperdynamic circulation and high cardiac output. Varices, ascites, splenomegaly/hypersplenism and encephalopathy are complications. Variceal bleeding is treated with vasoactive drugs, antibiotics, endoscopic banding and careful resuscitation. If there are varices with normal liver and synthetic function and splenomegaly, portal/splenic vein thrombosis or noncirrhotic portal hypertension is checked with Doppler. Child-Pugh requires bilirubin, albumin, INR, ascites and encephalopathy and cannot be calculated without all data.

questions.question_en: A 41-year-old man presented with abdominal pain that started last night. He has vomited twice. His pain worsens when he lies down and improves when he bends forward. In the examination of the abdomen, intestinal sounds are reduced and tenderness is evident in the upper part of the abdomen. A bruised spot (ecchymosis) can be seen on the patient's left phalanx. In laboratory examination, serum calcium is low and metabolic acidosis is moderate. Which of the following steps will help to confirm the diagnosis?

questions.explanation_en: Acute pancreatitis is diagnosed with epigastric pain radiating to back and lipase/amylase more than three times or imaging. The primary treatment is goal-directed lactated Ringer, analgesia and early oral/enteral feeding; A fixed volume of 5-6 liters is dangerous for everyone. Antibiotic prophylaxis is prohibited in sterile necrosis. infected necrosis is managed with antibiotic penetrating necrosis and step-up approach including drainage and delayed minimally invasive necrosectomy; Immediate open surgery is usually not preferred. In mild biliary pancreatitis, cholecystectomy reduces same admission recurrence and ERCP requires only cholangitis/ongoing obstruction.

questions.explanation_en: Chronic pancreatitis, especially with alcohol, causes pancreatic exocrine insufficiency, smelly/bulky steatorrhea, weight loss, and fat-soluble vitamin deficiency. Fecal elastase is a non-invasive test and secretin stimulation is more sensitive but invasive/hardly available. Treatment is alcohol/smoking cessation, pancreatic enzymes along with food and nutrition. High pleural fluid amylase is seen in pancreatitis/pseudocyst, esophageal rupture and some malignancies, and TB is less important. Acute pancreatitis with early enteral feeding, analgesia and fluid goal-directed management and antibiotic prophylaxis is not routine.

The primary treatment is goal-directed lactated Ringer, analgesia and early oral/enteral feeding; A fixed volume of 5-6 liters is dangerous for everyone. questions.explanation_en: In acute diarrhea, dehydration, sepsis, blood, high fever, age and immune status are evaluated first. Most short-term watery cases are treated with ORS and continued feeding, and antibiotics or routine stool testing are not required. Stool culture/PCR is relevant in dysentery, severe fever, severe dehydration, outbreak, immunocompromise, old age or persistence, and C. difficile testing after antibiotic/hospitalization. Loperamide is avoided in bloody diarrhea, high fever or suspected invasive infection. Diagnostic workup should not delay rehydration.

questions.explanation_en: H. pylori is detected by urea breath test or active stool antigen and its eradication is confirmed by non-serological test at least four weeks after antibiotic and two weeks after stopping PPI. IgG remains positive for months/years after treatment and is not a test-of-cure. The choice of regimen depends on clarithromycin resistance and previous exposure; bismuth quadruple therapy is the preferred empirical choice in many areas. gastric ulcer should have endoscopy and biopsy from the edge to rule out malignancy and follow-up healing; Simple duodenal ulcer is more benign. Visible vessel bleeding ulcer requires endoscopic treatment and high-dose IV PPI.

questions.explanation_en: In GI bleeding, first ABC, two IV, type/cross, CBC/coag and resuscitation are performed; Endoscopy is not performed before hemodynamic stabilization. Hematochezia with shock and very high BUN/Cr can be upper GI brisk bleeding, and upper endoscopy is the priority after stabilization. In persistent lower bleeding, colonoscopy after bowel prep; In ongoing brisk bleed, CT angiography and then embolization is useful. A visible hemorrhoid in a person over 45 or with anemia/change bowel habit does not rule out cancer and colonoscopy is necessary. NSAID raises bleeding risk and melena upper source.

questions.explanation_en: SAAG = serum albumin − ascitic albumin; A value of ≥1.1 indicates portal hypertension. High protein ascites with high SAAG leads to cardiac ascites, Budd-Chiari or early sinusoidal disease, and low protein leads to cirrhosis. SBP is diagnosed with PMN≥250/mm³ and treated immediately with cefotaxime/ceftriaxone; Bedside culture is taken before antibiotic. IV albumin in SBP with renal dysfunction/high bilirubin reduces the risk of HRS, but criteria are needed. Routine endoscopy is not an immediate action for an SBP episode unless there is a separate bleeding/screening indication.

questions.explanation_en: In acute HBV, HBsAg and anti-HBc IgM are positive and anti-HBs is negative; HBeAg shows proliferation but may be negative in precore mutant. The window period is known only with anti-HBc IgM and isolated anti-HBs after vaccination. Acute hepatitis B is often treated in supportive adults; Antiviral is selected for acute liver failure or severe/protracted disease. PT/INR, mental status, glucose and bilirubin determine the severity. HBV DNA is important for baseline/chronic disease management, not a requirement for acute serological diagnosis in all patients.

questions.explanation_en: In GI bleeding, first ABC, two IV, type/cross, CBC/coag and resuscitation are performed; Endoscopy is not performed before hemodynamic stabilization. Hematochezia with shock and very high BUN/Cr can be upper GI brisk bleeding, and upper endoscopy is the priority after stabilization. In persistent lower bleeding, colonoscopy after bowel prep; In ongoing brisk bleed, CT angiography and then embolization is useful. A visible hemorrhoid in a person over 45 or with anemia/change bowel habit does not rule out cancer and colonoscopy is necessary. NSAID raises bleeding risk and melena upper source.

questions.explanation_en: Chronic pancreatitis, especially with alcohol, causes pancreatic exocrine insufficiency, smelly/bulky steatorrhea, weight loss, and fat-soluble vitamin deficiency. Fecal elastase is a non-invasive test and secretin stimulation is more sensitive but invasive/hardly available. Treatment is alcohol/smoking cessation, pancreatic enzymes along with food and nutrition. High pleural fluid amylase is seen in pancreatitis/pseudocyst, esophageal rupture and some malignancies, and TB is less important. Acute pancreatitis with early enteral feeding, analgesia and fluid goal-directed management and antibiotic prophylaxis is not routine.

questions.explanation_en: SAAG = serum albumin − ascitic albumin; A value of ≥1.1 indicates portal hypertension. High protein ascites with high SAAG leads to cardiac ascites, Budd-Chiari or early sinusoidal disease, and low protein leads to cirrhosis. SBP is diagnosed with PMN≥250/mm³ and treated immediately with cefotaxime/ceftriaxone; Bedside culture is taken before antibiotic. IV albumin in SBP with renal dysfunction/high bilirubin reduces the risk of HRS, but criteria are needed. Routine endoscopy is not an immediate action for an SBP episode unless there is a separate bleeding/screening indication.

questions.explanation_en: Acute pancreatitis is diagnosed with epigastric pain radiating to back and lipase/amylase more than three times or imaging. The primary treatment is goal-directed lactated Ringer, analgesia and early oral/enteral feeding; A fixed volume of 5-6 liters is dangerous for everyone. Antibiotic prophylaxis is prohibited in sterile necrosis. infected necrosis is managed with antibiotic penetrating necrosis and step-up approach including drainage and delayed minimally invasive necrosectomy; Immediate open surgery is usually not preferred. In mild biliary pancreatitis, cholecystectomy reduces same admission recurrence and ERCP requires only cholangitis/ongoing obstruction.

questions.explanation_en: Chronic pancreatitis, especially with alcohol, causes pancreatic exocrine insufficiency, smelly/bulky steatorrhea, weight loss, and fat-soluble vitamin deficiency. Fecal elastase is a non-invasive test and secretin stimulation is more sensitive but invasive/hardly available. Treatment is alcohol/smoking cessation, pancreatic enzymes along with food and nutrition. High pleural fluid amylase is seen in pancreatitis/pseudocyst, esophageal rupture and some malignancies, and TB is less important. Acute pancreatitis with early enteral feeding, analgesia and fluid goal-directed management and antibiotic prophylaxis is not routine.

Hematochezia with shock and very high BUN/Cr can be upper GI brisk bleeding, and upper endoscopy is the priority after stabilization. In persistent lower bleeding, colonoscopy after bowel prep; In ongoing brisk bleed, CT angiography and then embolization is useful. A visible hemorrhoid in a person over 45 or with anemia/change bowel habit does not rule out cancer and colonoscopy is necessary. NSAID raises bleeding risk and melena upper source.

questions.explanation_en: H. pylori is detected by urea breath test or active stool antigen and its eradication is confirmed by non-serological test at least four weeks after antibiotic and two weeks after stopping PPI. IgG remains positive for months/years after treatment and is not a test-of-cure. Visible vessel bleeding ulcer requires endoscopic treatment and high-dose IV PPI.

questions.explanation_en: H. pylori is detected by urea breath test or active stool antigen and its eradication is confirmed by non-serological test at least four weeks after antibiotic and two weeks after stopping PPI. IgG remains positive for months/years after treatment and is not a test-of-cure. The choice of regimen depends on clarithromycin resistance and previous exposure; bismuth quadruple therapy is the preferred empirical choice in many areas. gastric ulcer should have endoscopy and biopsy from the edge to rule out malignancy and follow-up healing; Simple duodenal ulcer is more benign. Visible vessel bleeding ulcer requires endoscopic treatment and high-dose IV PPI.

questions.explanation_en: In acute HBV, HBsAg and anti-HBc IgM are positive and anti-HBs is negative; HBeAg shows proliferation but may be negative in precore mutant. The window period is known only with anti-HBc IgM and isolated anti-HBs after vaccination. Acute hepatitis B is often treated in supportive adults; Antiviral is selected for acute liver failure or severe/protracted disease. PT/INR, mental status, glucose and bilirubin determine the severity. HBV DNA is important for baseline/chronic disease management, not a requirement for acute serological diagnosis in all patients.

questions.explanation_en: SAAG = serum albumin − ascitic albumin; A value of ≥1.1 indicates portal hypertension. High protein ascites with high SAAG leads to cardiac ascites, Budd-Chiari or early sinusoidal disease, and low protein leads to cirrhosis. SBP is diagnosed with PMN≥250/mm³ and treated immediately with cefotaxime/ceftriaxone; Bedside culture is taken before antibiotic. IV albumin in SBP with renal dysfunction/high bilirubin reduces the risk of HRS, but criteria are needed. Routine endoscopy is not an immediate action for an SBP episode unless there is a separate bleeding/screening indication.

Empiric steroid without diagnosis is dangerous. questions.explanation_en: In GI bleeding, first ABC, two IV, type/cross, CBC/coag and resuscitation are performed; Endoscopy is not performed before hemodynamic stabilization. Hematochezia with shock and very high BUN/Cr can be upper GI brisk bleeding, and upper endoscopy is the priority after stabilization. In persistent lower bleeding, colonoscopy after bowel prep; In ongoing brisk bleed, CT angiography and then embolization is useful. A visible hemorrhoid in a person over 45 or with anemia/change bowel habit does not rule out cancer and colonoscopy is necessary. NSAID raises bleeding risk and melena upper source.

questions.explanation_en: Asymptomatic gallstones usually require observation, and prophylactic cholecystectomy is considered only in selected conditions such as porcelain gallbladder, large polyp, hemolytic anemia, or specific transplant/high-risk. Obesity, rapid weight loss, female sex and cirrhosis increase the risk of stones. Acute cholecystitis with RUQ pain, fever, Murphy and wall thickening/stones requires early laparoscopic cholecystectomy treatment. Renal failure is not the only indication for prophylactic surgery. UDCA is selected for small cholesterol stones in non-surgical patients with high recurrence.

questions.explanation_en: H. pylori is detected by urea breath test or active stool antigen and its eradication is confirmed by non-serological test at least four weeks after antibiotic and two weeks after stopping PPI. IgG remains positive for months/years after treatment and is not a test-of-cure. The choice of regimen depends on clarithromycin resistance and previous exposure; bismuth quadruple therapy is the preferred empirical choice in many areas. gastric ulcer should have endoscopy and biopsy from the edge to rule out malignancy and follow-up healing; Simple duodenal ulcer is more benign. Visible vessel bleeding ulcer requires endoscopic treatment and high-dose IV PPI.

questions.explanation_en: Asymptomatic gallstones usually require observation, and prophylactic cholecystectomy is considered only in selected conditions such as porcelain gallbladder, large polyp, hemolytic anemia, or specific transplant/high-risk. Obesity, rapid weight loss, female sex and cirrhosis increase the risk of stones. Acute cholecystitis with RUQ pain, fever, Murphy and wall thickening/stones requires early laparoscopic cholecystectomy treatment. Renal failure is not the only indication for prophylactic surgery. UDCA is selected for small cholesterol stones in non-surgical patients with high recurrence.

questions.explanation_en: Average-risk CRC screening starts at the age of 45. In first-degree relative with CRC or advanced adenoma before age 60, colonoscopy is recommended starting at age 40 or 10 years earlier than family diagnosis—whichever is earlier—and every 5 years. If the mother is infected at the age of 26, hereditary syndrome such as Lynch/FAP should be investigated with genetic counseling and the usual options may not be correct. CEA is not enough for initial screening/diagnosis, but it is useful for baseline prognostic and surveillance after treatment. Rectal bleeding in old age with hemorrhoids also requires colon evaluation.

questions.explanation_en: SAAG = serum albumin − ascitic albumin; A value of ≥1.1 indicates portal hypertension. High protein ascites with high SAAG leads to cardiac ascites, Budd-Chiari or early sinusoidal disease, and low protein leads to cirrhosis. SBP is diagnosed with PMN≥250/mm³ and treated immediately with cefotaxime/ceftriaxone; Bedside culture is taken before antibiotic. IV albumin in SBP with renal dysfunction/high bilirubin reduces the risk of HRS, but criteria are needed. Routine endoscopy is not an immediate action for an SBP episode unless there is a separate bleeding/screening indication.

questions.explanation_en: Acute pancreatitis is diagnosed with epigastric pain radiating to back and lipase/amylase more than three times or imaging. The primary treatment is goal-directed lactated Ringer, analgesia and early oral/enteral feeding; A fixed volume of 5-6 liters is dangerous for everyone. Antibiotic prophylaxis is prohibited in sterile necrosis. infected necrosis is managed with antibiotic penetrating necrosis and step-up approach including drainage and delayed minimally invasive necrosectomy; Immediate open surgery is usually not preferred. In mild biliary pancreatitis, cholecystectomy reduces same admission recurrence and ERCP requires only cholangitis/ongoing obstruction.

Hematochezia with shock and very high BUN/Cr can be upper GI brisk bleeding, and upper endoscopy is the priority after stabilization. The window period is known only with anti-HBc IgM and isolated anti-HBs after vaccination. questions.explanation_en: In GI bleeding, first ABC, two IV, type/cross, CBC/coag and resuscitation are performed; Endoscopy is not performed before hemodynamic stabilization. Hematochezia with shock and very high BUN/Cr can be upper GI brisk bleeding, and upper endoscopy is the priority after stabilization. In persistent lower bleeding, colonoscopy after bowel prep; In ongoing brisk bleed, CT angiography and then embolization is useful. A visible hemorrhoid in a person over 45 or with anemia/change bowel habit does not rule out cancer and colonoscopy is necessary. NSAID raises bleeding risk and melena upper source.

questions.explanation_en: Pruritus, direct hyperbilirubinemia and high ALP/GGT with ultrasound ducts suggest normal intrahepatic cholestasis. Most middle-aged women have PBC, AMA positive and small intrahepatic duct destruction; With cholestatic enzymes and AMA, biopsy is usually not required for diagnosis unless there is overlap/uncertainty. ERCP for obstruction/therapeutic intervention, not first-line diagnosis in uncomplicated PBC/PSC.

questions.explanation_en: SAAG = serum albumin − ascitic albumin; A value of ≥1.1 indicates portal hypertension. High protein ascites with high SAAG leads to cardiac ascites, Budd-Chiari or early sinusoidal disease, and low protein leads to cirrhosis. SBP is diagnosed with PMN≥250/mm³ and treated immediately with cefotaxime/ceftriaxone; Bedside culture is taken before antibiotic. IV albumin in SBP with renal dysfunction/high bilirubin reduces the risk of HRS, but criteria are needed. Routine endoscopy is not an immediate action for an SBP episode unless there is a separate bleeding/screening indication.

The primary treatment is goal-directed lactated Ringer, analgesia and early oral/enteral feeding; A fixed volume of 5-6 liters is dangerous for everyone. questions.explanation_fa:
تحلیل بالینی و صورت مسئله: در این سناریو، بیمار با تظاهرات «در عفونت HBV کسب شده در زمان تولد نسبت به عفونت HBV کسب شده در دوره ی بزرگسالی همه ی موارد زیر بیشتر اتفاق می افتد، بجز:» در حیطه تخصصی گوارش تحت ارزیابی قرار گرفته است. با استناد به مبانی تشخیصی و تصمیم‌گیری بالینی مرجع کانونی اصول طب داخلی هاریسون (ویرایش ۲۲)، بخش اختلالات دستگاه گوارش و کبد و پانکراس، اقدام انتخابی و پاسخ صحیح بالینی «هپاتیت حاد» می‌باشد.

پاتوفیزیولوژی و استدلال گایدلاین هاریسون: انتخاب «هپاتیت حاد» بر اساس رویکرد گام‌به‌گام طب مبتنی بر شواهد استوار است. این استراتژی درمانی/تشخیصی با هدف تثبیت وضعیت همودینامیک، مهار فرآیندهای پاتولوژیک زمینه‌ای و کاهش مورتالیتی و موربیدیتی ناشی از بیماری اتخاذ می‌گردد. در مدیریت بالینی این بیماری، توازن دقیق میان منافع مداخله و خطرات عوارض جانبی مطابق سرفصل‌های به‌روزشده هاریسون برقرار شده است.

ارزیابی تحلیلی گزینه‌های دیگر: سایر گزینه‌ها به دلیل اثربخشی کمتر، تطابق ناکافی با معیارهای قطعی راهنماهای بالینی، یا داشتن عوارض جانبی و تأخیر در روند بهبودی در مقایسه با «هپاتیت حاد» در اولویت بعدی قرار گرفته و رد می‌شوند.
questions.explanation_en: In acute HBV, HBsAg and anti-HBc IgM are positive and anti-HBs is negative; HBeAg shows proliferation but may be negative in precore mutant. The window period is known only with anti-HBc IgM and isolated anti-HBs after vaccination. Acute hepatitis B is often treated in supportive adults; Antiviral is selected for acute liver failure or severe/protracted disease. PT/INR, mental status, glucose and bilirubin determine the severity. HBV DNA is important for baseline/chronic disease management, not a requirement for acute serological diagnosis in all patients.

questions.explanation_en: Chronic pancreatitis, especially with alcohol, causes pancreatic exocrine insufficiency, smelly/bulky steatorrhea, weight loss, and fat-soluble vitamin deficiency. Fecal elastase is a non-invasive test and secretin stimulation is more sensitive but invasive/hardly available. Treatment is alcohol/smoking cessation, pancreatic enzymes along with food and nutrition. Acute pancreatitis with early enteral feeding, analgesia and fluid goal-directed management and antibiotic prophylaxis is not routine.

questions.explanation_en: Crohn's transmural and skip lesions from mouth to anus, terminal ileum is a common involvement and noncaseating granuloma is possible; Fistula, stricture, perianal disease and malabsorption are common. Massive lower GI bleeding can occur, but it is relatively less than other complications. UC is limited to mucosa/submucosa and continuous and has more toxic megacolon/pseudopolyps. questions.explanation_en: H. pylori is detected by urea breath test or active stool antigen and its eradication is confirmed by non-serological test at least four weeks after antibiotic and two weeks after stopping PPI. IgG remains positive for months/years after treatment and is not a test-of-cure. The choice of regimen depends on clarithromycin resistance and previous exposure; bismuth quadruple therapy is the preferred empirical choice in many areas. gastric ulcer should have endoscopy and biopsy from the edge to rule out malignancy and follow-up healing; Simple duodenal ulcer is more benign. Visible vessel bleeding ulcer requires endoscopic treatment and high-dose IV PPI.

questions.explanation_en: SAAG = serum albumin − ascitic albumin; A value of ≥1.1 indicates portal hypertension. High protein ascites with high SAAG leads to cardiac ascites, Budd-Chiari or early sinusoidal disease, and low protein leads to cirrhosis. SBP is diagnosed with PMN≥250/mm³ and treated immediately with cefotaxime/ceftriaxone; Bedside culture is taken before antibiotic. IV albumin in SBP with renal dysfunction/high bilirubin reduces the risk of HRS, but criteria are needed. Routine endoscopy is not an immediate action for an SBP episode unless there is a separate bleeding/screening indication.

questions.explanation_en: SAAG = serum albumin − ascitic albumin; A value of ≥1.1 indicates portal hypertension. questions.explanation_en: In acute diarrhea, dehydration, sepsis, blood, high fever, age and immune status are evaluated first. Most short-term watery cases are treated with ORS and continued feeding, and antibiotics or routine stool testing are not required. questions.explanation_fa:
تحلیل صورت سؤال: محور اصلی در حوزه «داخلی» و مبحث «گوارش» است. صورت سؤال «آقای 30 سالهای با سابقه ی 8 ه سال ی(اسهال) و یبوست متناوب همراه با درد شکم مراجع…» نکته کلیدی را در مرکز قرار می‌دهد. برای پاسخ باید یافته‌ها را با الگوریتم منبع: هاریسون ۲۲، فصل مربوطه تطبیق داد.

چرا «آندوسکوپی دستگاه گوارش فوقانی» صحیح است: آندوسکوپی دستگاه گوارش فوقانی (EGD) در یک جوان با سابقه اسهال و یبوست تناوبی بدون هیچ علامت هشدار یا شکایت فوقانی گوارشی هیچ کاربردی ندارد. این انتخاب دقیقاً با معیارهای تشخیصی منبع: هاریسون ۲۲، فصل مربوطه هم‌سو است و بیشترین سود با کمترین خطر را دارد.

رد سایر گزینه‌ها: گزینه 1 (آزمایش کامل مدفوع): آزمایش مدفوع برای رد عفونت‌ها یا خونریزی مخفی در ارزیابی اولیه اسهال مزمن مفید است.؛ گزینه 2 (شمارش سلولهای خون محیطی (CBC)): شمارش کامل سلول‌های خون (CBC) برای رد کم‌خونی و عفونت ضروری است.؛ گزینه 4 (رکتوسیگموئیدوسکوپی): سیگموئیدوسکوپی برای رد ضایعات…. هر یک یا با یافته‌های اصلی ناسازگار است یا در الگوریتم جایگاه بعدی دارد یا بدون مزیت اضافی خطر/هزینه می‌افزاید.

درسنامه فشرده (منبع: هاریسون ۲۲، فصل مربوطه): ابتدا پایداری همودینامیک، سپس شرح حال هدفمند و معاینه متمرکز، و تست‌های انتخابی بر اساس پیش‌آزمون. درمان بر پایه شدت، زمینه و ترجیح بیمار؛ پایش پاسخ و عوارض ضروری است.

نکته طلایی و دام: گزینه «درستِ ناقص» شایع‌ترین دام است؛ کامل‌ترین تطابق با رفرنس را انتخاب کنید. مراقب قیدهای «همیشه/هرگز» باشید — در پزشکی مطلق نادر است.
questions.explanation_en: Irritable bowel syndrome is defined by recurrent abdominal pain associated with defecation and change in stool frequency or shape, without explanatory structural damage. Warning signs include onset at an advanced age, weight loss, blood, anemia, fever, nocturnal diarrhea, family history of IBD/cancer, and elevated inflammatory markers and require organic investigation. Treatment is with education, soluble fiber such as psyllium, short-term guided low-FODMAP diet, antispasmodic, and subtype therapy; Rifaximin for IBS-D and low-dose TCA are useful in selected pain/IBS-D.
